_: Narration for video-short. One entry per scene id in ../video-short/index.html.
Rewritten 2026-09-16 to follow presentation/expo-deck.html scene for scene: the
copy-paste problem, publishing the kit, the two lanes, the IDE, the gates,
self-healing, the admin learning loop, the proof run (with its rehearsal caveat)
and the close. Short sentences, every term defined the first time it is used.
Numbers are spelled the way they should be spoken — the speech synthesiser
reads '98.5%' badly. Scenes stretch to hold the words (compose_film.py).
intro: This is Control Center. It takes a business requirement all the way to a governed release.
problem: Here is the problem. A developer copies a ticket and pastes it into the A.I. assistant in their editor. Three developers do it three different ways. One pastes the description. One pastes half and writes their own prompt. One pastes just the title. Same requirement, three different results, and nothing checks the result.
difference: So we stop pasting context, and publish it instead. Control Center builds one context kit from the approved plan: instructions for the assistant, the stories with their acceptance criteria, the architecture, and a failing test for every criterion. The kit goes into git, next to the code, and every developer's assistant reads the same files.
solution: The work has two halves. Upstream, the business and A.I. agree what done means. Downstream, developers and A.I. build until it is proven. The kit joins the two halves, and at five gates, a named person has to sign.
upstream: Upstream, the business uploads the requirement, and A.I. extracts it. A.I. breaks it into stories, each with numbered acceptance criteria. A named owner checks every item and signs, and the plan locks. Then the kit is published to git for every team.
ide: In the editor, the developer says: start working on story one. The assistant reads the kit, finds three criteria, and each one already has a failing test. The developer asks for a plan, edits it, and says: build the plan. The code is written, and the first test turns green.
gates: Every step is governed. Five gates, each signed by a named person. Twelve quality checks, computed from real evidence and never asked of a model. Nine conditions must pass before quality signs off. Nothing approves its own work.
heal: If something changes late, it cannot slip through. Everything built on the change goes stale, and a versioned playbook re-opens exactly the gates it touches, until every step is cleared again.
admin: And Control Center gets better. When a person corrects the A.I., the correction is captured. The admin panel drafts a better prompt, an operator accepts or rejects it, and every change lands as a new version, on the record.
proof: And it runs. In one overnight rehearsal, a brand new requirement went all the way to a released application. A real repository, a reviewer that blocked a story until it was fixed, a merged pull request, and ninety eight point five percent test coverage. One operator played every role, and every gate still waited for its signature.
outro: Governance is the product. Not how much the A.I. writes, but how many places a named person signs.
